question: Which type of muscle is voluntary and shows light and dark bands?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Striated muscle**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Striated muscles**, also commonly referred to as **skeletal muscles**, are primarily attached to the **bones** by **tendons** and are responsible for the **locomotion** and movement of the body.
 
• These muscles are characterized by the presence of alternating **light and dark bands** or **striations** when viewed under a microscope. These bands are formed due to the highly organized arrangement of **contractile proteins**, namely **Actin** (light bands) and **Myosin** (dark bands).
 
• Striated muscles are **voluntary** in nature, meaning their movement and contraction are under the **conscious control** of the individual. This control is mediated by the **somatic nervous system**.
 
• The **cells** (fibers) of striated muscles are **long**, **cylindrical**, and **unbranched**. A unique feature of these fibers is that they are **multinucleated**, containing many nuclei located at the periphery of the cell.
 
• They facilitate activities such as **walking**, **running**, **writing**, and **maintaining posture**. B
